finding: The cut of the spec-hash reset (a9a11af) removed §3 'A changed spec ends the streak' but left §1 Overview byte-identical to snapshot-round-5. §1 still reads: 'Two deliverables, and only the first is a no-op by default. §2 ships audit_converge_on ... §3 changes consecutive_clean and converged for any project whose spec moves between rounds, opted in or not. An earlier draft of this paragraph claimed the whole release was behaviour-preserving; it is not, and §3 is why.' §3 is now 'What this release deliberately does not contain' and changes nothing. The Overview therefore commissions the exact work the release deliberately cut, and denies the behaviour-preservation claim that is now true. An implementer reading §1 first will build the reset.
suggestion: Rewrite §1's third paragraph: one deliverable, behaviour-preserving by default, and point at §3 as the record of what was cut rather than as a second deliverable.

finding: Non-Goal 4 is unchanged from snapshot-round-5 and still reads '§3 adds a function rather than altering the shared one precisely so review's --status cannot move.' §3 adds no function now. The non-goal's entire warrant — that review's convergence is safe because the new work is additive — has been deleted along with the work, so the non-goal now rests on a mechanism that does not exist. Worse, it reads as spec cover for adding a function to the audit path.
suggestion: Restate Non-Goal 4 without §3: review's convergence is untouched because this release adds no new walk at all; the only new code is audit_converge_on's predicate, which review never reads.

finding: The 'One shipped guard is deliberately reversed' paragraph still justifies naming assertion ':498' by saying it is the one 'which §3's reset touches'. §3 has no reset. The reason the assertion is called out is now unsupported, and a reader can no longer tell whether :498 still needs protecting.
suggestion: Replace 'which §3's reset touches' with the reason that survives the cut — the streak-entry shape is what a severity-aware clean predicate would be tempted to widen — or drop the clause and keep the sweep-record citation alone.

finding: The same paragraph ends '§5 test 12 pins all nine.' §5 now lists eleven tests; the nine-assertions test is test 11. The reference points past the end of the list. (snapshot-round-5 said 'test 9', which was also wrong — it pointed at 'The shared walk does not move' — so a9a11af renumbered a reference that was already broken and landed on a different wrong number.)

finding: §2.2 closes '§5 test 5 uses a legacy row because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live.' §5 test 5 is now 'warning is advisory'; the test that uses a legacy row is test 7, 'Unrecognised fails closed'. a9a11af bumped this pointer by one while inserting two new tests ahead of it, so it moved from wrong-by-one (snapshot said test 4) to wrong-by-two.

finding: a6d80f1 corrected the two sweep targets but left §2 asserting the defect is still live, pinned to line numbers whose content it changed. §2 still says the five-layer form 'still stands in two other places this release must sweep: skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:519-522 states it as *the* rule for workflow fields, and spec/0.31.0.md:41 carries it for the twin', and that 'REFERENCE.md:327-328 additionally names TP_RUN_MAX_UNITS and TP_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS'. Drop the three line-number pins, which cannot survive the repair they describe.

finding: The precedence correction over-generalized and broke a statement that was right. §2's field-scoped claim (configresolve.go:261 merges two layers — verified correct) was carried into skills/tp/REFERENCE.md as an absolute: ':527-529 No workflow field has a CLI flag or a TP_<FIELD> environment layer ... for every one of them', and ':327-330 workflow fields have no env layer to ignore'. Both are falsified by tp's own production source and by REFERENCE.md itself. internal/engine/runnerseam.go is production code: SeamRunner reads TP_RUNNER_SEAM and ResolveUnitRunner (runnertemplate.go:289-301) reads it FIRST, short-circuiting the runner workflow field entirely; runnerseam.go:12-16's own comment calls it an override that 'outranks a CLI flag'. REFERENCE.md:503 — 24 lines above the corrected block — still says exactly that. And spec/0.35.0.md:568-573, the passage a6d80f1 deliberately left as the historical record, is MORE correct than the corrected files: it states the same rule and then names the two exceptions (notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only; TP_RUNNER_SEAM outranks every layer). The correction deleted an exception list that was right.
suggestion: Restore the exceptions in both REFERENCE.md sites: no workflow field has a CLI flag or a TP_<FIELD> layer, EXCEPT that notify_cmd resolves from .tp/local.json only and TP_RUNNER_SEAM is a test-only override of runner that outranks every layer. Copy the wording from spec/0.35.0.md:571-573 rather than re-deriving it. §2 should say the sweep must preserve them, since it is the sentence that commissioned the sweep.

finding: §2's newly added 'blocking governs clean and nothing else' paragraph refutes Non-Goal 6's premise. Non-Goal 6 says 'Under blocking, a clean round can have surviving warning and info rows and tp emits no count of them, so an agent reading clean: true cannot tell an empty round from a suppressed one.' §2 now says the opposite: role_streaks[].open is computed through AuditRowIsPass alone, so 'under blocking a round can therefore record clean: true beside a non-zero open'. tp does emit a count, and under blocking a clean round's survivors are all non-blocking by definition, so open IS exactly the nonblocking count for precisely the rounds Non-Goal 6 is about. clean:true with open>0 is the suppressed-round signal Non-Goal 6 claims does not exist.
suggestion: Narrow Non-Goal 6's premise: the gap is not that no count exists but that no count is scoped to the non-blocking survivors and named as such on the payload, and role_streaks[].open is a per-role count an agent must sum. Keep the deferral, whose real warrant is the pinned-guard inversion, and drop the refuted sentence.

finding: Non-Goal 6 states that its own earlier count of six 'was copied into spec/0.46.0.md before anyone checked it', and the sweep did not go and fix it. spec/0.46.0.md:330-332 still reads 'six places pin its absence on the audit side by name — spec/0.31.0.md §8.4 and its test 18, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:634, skills/tp/SKILL.md, reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go:185-205, harness_note_test.go:263.' I verified §4's refutation and it is right: harness_note_test.go:258-299 is TestCompact_AuditOmitsHarnessKeepsNextAction, whose only mention of the field is the comment at :263 and whose body asserts nothing about it; SKILL.md names it only at :72 and :76, both review contexts. So a release spec now knowingly leaves a falsified count standing in the spec that inherits the item — the exact class this repository's 'never assert a quantifier you did not count' rule exists for, and §8.3 is where the next cycle will read it.
suggestion: Correct spec/0.46.0.md §8.3 to four in the same batch, with the two exclusions and their reasons, and delete the parenthetical from §4 once it has nothing left to warn about. A claim a sibling spec is told is false and left standing is worse than the original error.

finding: §3 hands the reset to spec/0.46.0.md §8.4, but §8.4 contradicts the two statements that define what that file holds. Its header says the items there 'have a different provenance — v0.36.0's own audit rounds' and that 'Round 8 added one more after the split; the rest is unchanged'; §1 says each item was 'measured to a conclusion during v0.36.0's audit and each deliberately not repaired there'. §8.4's provenance is v0.37.0's review rounds 3-5, it was not measured during v0.36.0's audit, and it is a second post-split addition. §8.4 also sits under a §8 heading whose subject is 'the gate tp reports and the gate this project ships on are not the same gate' — §8.1-§8.3 are all about which rows block, and §8.4 is about a streak invalidated by a moving spec, which is a different question.
suggestion: Either give the reset its own top-level section in spec/0.46.0.md (§8c, beside §8a and §8b, which are also post-split additions) or amend that file's header and §1 to say two items arrived from spec/0.37.0.md's review with their own provenance. §3 should name whichever anchor results.

finding: Two near-misses, both recorded because the second is a tooling hazard the next round will meet. (1) The unit prompt asked whether the precedence correction broke REFERENCE.md's split by field kind, 'particularly no_color, since no_color really does have flag and env layers'. It did not: REFERENCE.md:525 keeps the output-defaults chain and :539 keeps no_color's explicit precedence, and the two agree. I was one step from reporting the primed hypothesis, which would have been a false finding AND would have hidden the real break, which is on runner and notify_cmd 24 lines away and was not named in the prompt. Checking the two lines the correction did not touch is what separated them. (2) faster_search with mode=regex and pattern '0\.37\.0' returned 0 matches over the whole repository, where the literal 'spec/0.37.0.md' returns 16 across 8 files. I nearly concluded from that zero that nothing in the tree references this spec — which would have answered the prompt's fourth question with a fabricated negative. Escaped dots are not honoured by the zigrep_basic flavour; use mode=literal for any question whose answer is an absence.
suggestion: No spec change. Recorded so the next round does not re-run the regex form, and so the no_color result is not re-derived: it is correct and needs no repair.

finding: The fence paragraph was rewritten in this batch and the rewrite built a cost estimate on a premise the source refutes. It claims 'the only workflow-write fence is fenceWorkflowWrite(field string, requested float64) in internal/cli/unattended.go:56 — numeric by signature, covering caps and command fields. A string-valued field does not fit it', and concludes 'Widening it is two new call sites in two files.' A second, entirely string-shaped workflow-write fence already exists and is already deployed at the two files this release must touch: set.go:361-362 and set_project.go:46-47 both run 'if engine.Unattended() && engine.FencedCommandField(field) { refuseUnattendedCommandField(field) }' BEFORE the type dispatch — before ParseFloat/Atoi and before the unknown-field reply — and set_local.go:41-42 is a third instance. refuseUnattended(what, decision string) at unattended.go:33 takes no number at all. Two consequences the estimate gets wrong: the release does not widen a numeric fence, it adds a third predicate beside engine.FencedCapField/FencedCommandField plus one guard modelled on set.go:361, placed before the numeric branches rather than inside them. And fenceWorkflowWrite's own FencedCommandField branch (unattended.go:60-63) is unreachable from all four of its call sites, since a runner or notify_cmd value never survives ParseFloat/Atoi and the earlier guards catch it first — so it covers caps only, not 'caps and command fields'.
suggestion: Replace the paragraph's premise: tp already fences string-valued workflow fields, at set.go:361 and set_project.go:46, and audit_converge_on takes the same shape one predicate over. Keep the four fenceWorkflowWrite call sites as evidence that the NUMERIC fence is unreachable for a string field, which is still true and is why the existing guard is the right model. §5 test 9's two-path requirement is unaffected and should stand.

finding: a9a11af strengthened §5's opening from 'Every test names the input that makes it fail, because four earlier drafts...' to 'Every test names the input that makes it fail. Five earlier drafts of this list each contained a test that passed against unmodified tp, so the naming is not decoration: it is the check that the test has a failing arm at all' — and then added a test that names none. Test 3, 'The two surfaces v0.31.1 exists for', gives a reason for existing ('tested because v0.31.0 shipped the twin without them') where every other new test gives a killing mutation. It is the item most exposed to the failure the rule was written against: 'tp config --extract emits the field' passes vacuously if extract walks the workflow struct, and 'tp validate --project accepts it' passes vacuously if validate accepts unknown keys, so both arms can be green against an audit_converge_on that resolves nowhere. Tests 5 and 11 also state rationale rather than an input, but only test 3 is new and only test 3 can pass while the field is unwired.
suggestion: Give test 3 its failing arm: --extract must emit the field on a project whose task file sets it and validate --project must REJECT audit_converge_on=sometimes with the hint shape, so a resolver that never registered the field reddens both. Keep the strengthened rule; it is the right rule.
